Tilted OpenStreetMap with zero-drift HTML markers and PNG export

I wanted to know if a tilted 3D OpenStreetMap canvas could hold live HTML place cards with zero pan or zoom drift, real 3D building occlusion, keyboard Tab navigation and one-click PNG export. Drag the map to pan, right-drag (or use two fingers) to rotate, tilt the pitch slider, press Tab to step across pins, or export the whole scene into one PNG.

Show the code OpenStreetMap tile atlas, 3D building extrusions, depth-occluded DOM cards and PNG export
  1. Four place cards inside the canvas. Each landmark card is a drawable child of <canvas content="drawable" layoutsubtree> with buttons, a tag <select> and an editable visit note <input>.
  2. OpenStreetMap tile cache and offline atlas. A plain offscreen 2D canvas draws a procedural street-and-river base and composites cached crossOrigin = 'anonymous' tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org before uploading one texture to WebGL 2.
  3. 3D extruded landmark buildings and shaders. Shaded prisms sit at real city coordinates and write to the depth buffer so tilting and rotating the map hides pins behind taller towers.
  4. One WebGL 2 pass with depth occlusion and hit boxes. Ground tiles, buildings, pin stems and ElementGL cards share one camera matrix, then updateElementGeometry() and geometryUnit() sync every card's hit box.
  5. Tap-triggered PNG export. On click, the page draws a fresh frame, copies the canvas into a plain 2D canvas with drawImage(), adds attribution, calls toDataURL('image/png') and retires the temporary canvas.
  6. Texture upload in element-gl.js. texElementSubImage2D() copies each card into a texture sized to getElementImageDefaultSize().

How it works

Web maps usually pick between two awkward marker models. Libraries like Leaflet (L.divIcon) and MapLibre GL (maplibregl.Marker) float HTML pins in a sibling DOM layer above the canvas, which keeps forms and keyboard Tab focus working, though pins can lag behind the GPU camera during fast pans or pitches, can't be occluded by 3D buildings, and disappear when you call canvas.toDataURL(). Moving markers into a WebGL symbol layer fixes drift and export, yet gives up real inputs, buttons and Tab order.

Here I put four live HTML place cards inside one <canvas content="drawable" layoutsubtree> and render everything through a single ElementGL WebGL 2 context, building on the shared-context pattern from /relief-map/ and the projective hit-test matrix from /three-form/. OpenStreetMap raster tiles (https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png, © OpenStreetMap contributors) load with img.crossOrigin = 'anonymous' into an in-memory cache and composite onto one plain 1,280 by 1,280 offscreen 2D canvas. While tiles arrive (or if you're offline), that atlas draws a procedural street grid, parks and river geometry for London, Tokyo and San Francisco so the ground plane is never blank.

On each paint event, the ground quad, the extruded 3D landmark buildings, the pin stems and the four uploaded DOM cards all project through the same view-projection matrix derived from Web Mercator coordinates. Because ElementGL transforms each card quad with that matrix, leaving DEPTH_TEST enabled makes the GPU depth buffer occlude cards pixel-by-pixel behind closer 3D towers; unchecking "3D building occlusion" disables depth testing before the card pass so cards float in front. After drawing each card, updateElementGeometry() receives the element-to-canvas projective matrix scaled by geometryUnit(), and toggles data-hit-tick whenever the matrix changes to clear Chromium's hit-test cache.

Pressing Tab steps natively through every button, select and note input inside the canvas; a focusin listener highlights that card's stem and smoothly pans the map so the focused pin moves into view. Clicking "Export PNG" draws a fresh frame, copies the canvas into a plain 2D canvas with drawImage(), stamps the OpenStreetMap credit, generates a PNG data URL and retires the copy canvas immediately.

Findings

  • Drawing the tilted tile plane, 3D building prisms, pin stems and ElementGL DOM quads through one view-projection matrix eliminates marker pan/zoom lag because both map geometry and card textures commit in the same WebGL 2 frame.
  • Because ElementGL's vertex shader outputs uMatrix * vec4(aPos, 0.0, 1.0) directly into clip space, keeping DEPTH_TEST on with depthMask(false) during back-to-front card drawing gives true pixel-accurate occlusion behind 3D buildings without modifying element-gl.js.
  • Loading OpenStreetMap tiles with crossOrigin = 'anonymous' into a plain offscreen 2D atlas canvas keeps the WebGL texture untainted, so copying the composited frame to a plain 2D canvas on tap exports map tiles, 3D buildings and live HTML cards into one PNG.
  • Credits: map imagery and attribution come from OpenStreetMap contributors; the marker trade-off draws on Leaflet (L.divIcon) and MapLibre GL (maplibregl.Marker); the single-context ElementGL and projective hit-test setup builds on /relief-map/ and /three-form/.
  • Not verified yet: live browser runs in headless Chromium 157 and on Chrome 159 for Android (412 px touch pan, two-finger twist and pinch zoom, live CORS OpenStreetMap tile fetch, keyboard Tab traversal across drawable pins, and tap PNG export). Running the live checks above and testing on a device will verify those paths.
